J1.text: BendHub holds 1107 packages, 305 names, 61 authors and 18 posts; the oldest package is from 2026-09-10, so the hub is about two months old.

J2.text: Only 135 packages (12%) ship LAWS.bend and 136 (12%) PROOF.bend, so 88% carry none of the proofs Bend is pitched on.

J3.text: 257 packages (23%) ship their own .c or .js files, which the API docs say Bend runs without checking; publishing needs no account.

J4.text: Adoption is concentrated: paymog owns 48 of the 128 names sampled, and 310 of the 322 packages importing the most-imported name (bend-kit-bytes) are bend-kit's own; 730 packages (66%) give no source repository.

J5.text: The only testing packages are bend-kit-property (property checks with shrinking: 3 files, 0 dependents, 0 mentions, no LAWS or PROOF) and an unnamed 'bendcheck'; a search for 'assert' finds nothing.

J6.text: bend is not installed here; codelarpers runs stage tests as test.py, test.sh, test.mjs, test.js or an executable test (course.rs:244), and its starter kits are rust, go, python, javascript, typescript, c and cpp, with no Bend.

J7.text: Bend itself is v2.0.39 and its site says it is still evolving and to expect bugs.

P1.text: Write stage tests that need generated inputs with bend-kit-property, so a learner's failure shrinks to the smallest input that breaks their program.

evidence.source: bend-kit-property description: reproducible property checks with generated inputs and greedy shrinking

P2.text: Add a bend starter kit so codelarpers can host courses written in Bend, with hub packages as the libraries learners import and, where they cite a public repo and licence, as tutorial code examples; packages are content-addressed and never change, so an example's URL stays valid.

evidence.source: https://hub.bend-lang.com/guide (packages named by content hash, never change; default licence MIT-0)

P3.text: Get the same shrinking benefit without Bend: add property checks with greedy shrinking to the embedded Python helper (codelarpers_test), which needs nothing new on the learner's machine.

evidence.source: codelarpers_test already has a seeded random; a greedy shrinker over lists and strings is a small loop

O1.text: Every learner would need the Bend toolchain (curl | sh) and an executable test wrapper just to run stage tests, in courses written in Rust, Python or Go that never otherwise touch Bend.

O2.text: The ecosystem is two months old and mostly one author's family; the one testing package has no users, and versions churn fast (bend-kit-http is at 0.38 within about six weeks), so a course pinned to a package today is likely pinned to an abandoned one soon.

O3.text: As code examples, most packages fail the skill's rule of real code someone shipped: 66% name no source repository, authorship cannot be checked, and 23% run unchecked native code.

O4.text: Shrinking is the only thing P1 adds, and it needs no Bend: the learner-facing gain is a smaller failing input in the log, which the Python helper can produce.

O5.text: Each authoring agent would have to load Bend's guide before writing a Bend test or course, on top of the course's own research.

evidence.source: bend-lang.com: agents are told to run `bend guide`, which prints the whole language

O6.text: Use hub packages only inside a course that teaches Bend, and only packages that name a public source repository and licence; never in the harness or in other languages' tests.
